text:
zoe: Noticing a wave of tiny-gpu pods stuck Pending -> then Evicted in ap-southeast1 since 09:02 UTC. Symptoms: Attach delay -> scheduler drops packing and spreads pods.
infra-bot: ALERT GPU_VOLUME_ATTACH_ERRORS ap-southeast1 count=12 window=10m
liam: Can you grab one pod's events? `kubectl get pod train-lite-7 -n ml -o yaml` + events.
zoe: events snippet:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age    From               Message
  ----     ------             ----   ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled          3m     default-scheduler  Assigned to node-ap-se1-23
  Warning  FailedAttachVolume 2m     attach-detacher    rpc timeout after 40s
  Warning  Failed             1m     kubelet            Evicted: Preemption by higher priority
```
devon: Attach latency p99 is jumping to ~2m in that region per LiProm. Also seeing host egress QDisc drops on that host pool. If CSI attach exceeds preempt window we lose the allocate/bind atomicity and scheduler reconsiders other nodes.
sre-oncall: Quick actions I can take now: 1) widen attach grace in preemption controller to 90s for this region (temp), 2) increase warm-pool size by 30% (from 12 -> 16), 3) toggle the strict anti-affinity label `gpu:exclusive` from required -> preferred for ns=ml. Which should we do first?
liam: I'd add (4) restart csi-plugin controller on 4 nodes rotated to avoid wide disruption. Often long-lived controller grpc sessions leak.
zoe: Do (2) and (4) in parallel, then (1) if we still see evictions. We should avoid affinity toggles unless last resort.
liam: Crafting PromQL to watch attach latency: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(csi_attach_duration_seconds_bucket{region="ap-southeast1"}[5m])) by (le))` and attach errors: `sum(rate(csi_attach_errors_total{region="ap-southeast1"}[5m]))`
devon: Ran those -> attach p99 ~115s, errors=0.6/min. Warm pool egress bandwidth from the autoscaler hosts shows spikes aligning with attach spikes.
sre-oncall: Warm pool increased to 16, CSI controller restarted on canary nodes (node-ap-se1-23/24/25). Monitoring.
infra-bot: NOTE Incident INC-2024-839 opened for ap-southeast1 attach surge
zoe: After warm-pool + CSI restart: pending count down ~45% in 10m and evictions drop. But packing density still low; scheduler keeps preferring spread because of `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` anti-affinity rule on `workload=small-gpu` deployments.
liam: Propose a short-lived scheduler tweak: deploy a scoring plugin in canary that gives +15 score to nodes with free PCI affinity and >0.5 GPUs free so tiny pods prefer co-locating. Will run in ml-canary namespace.
devon: Also propose increasing CSI attach timeout default to 120s (kubelet/driver config) so attach stalls don't immediately trigger eviction windows. Need an RFC to change across clusters.
sre-oncall: Implemented canary scheduler scoring tweak for ml-canary. Observed packing density up ~30% on canary within 5m.
zoe: Great. Please keep the warm pool elevated for 90m total. We'll roll back scoring tweak after 1h of stable metrics.
liam: Filed short RFC draft: 1743100015 - "Increase CSI attach timeout + scheduler packing preference for tiny GPUs" with rollout checklist.
sre-oncall: Follow-ups: add runbook step to rotate CSI controller every 24h if p99 attach >45s, add alert: `csi_attach_p99 > 45s for 5m` to page SRE, and add metric for packing-density (pods_per_gpu_node) per AZ.
zoe: Postmortem notes for tomorrow: probable root cause = transient egress saturation on warm-pool hosts causing CSI attach RPCs to timeout; amplifiers = strict anti-affinity + short preempt window + conservative scheduler scoring. Mitigations applied = warm-pool bump, CSI controller rotation on canary, scheduler canary scoring, temporary attach-grace if needed.
infra-bot: RESOLVED: incident INC-2024-839 -> status=monitoring.
sre-oncall: Reverting anti-affinity not needed for now. We'll keep tests running and prepare RFC for permanent scheduler plugin.
zoe: Thanks team, will sync in ops sync 11:00 APAC to walk through RFC and followups. :white_check_mark:
